title: OpenAI announces the Admin plugin for ChatGPT Work and Codex
snippet: OpenAI’s new ChatGPT Admin plugin lets workspace admins manage users and permissions, analyze usage, and build reports directly from a conversation. Here are the details.
fullText:
OpenAI’s new ChatGPT Admin plugin lets workspace admins manage users and permissions, analyze usage, and build reports directly from a conversation. Here are the details.

Admin plugin operates within account permissions

OpenAI today announced the Admin plugin for ChatGPT Work and Codex, a new tool that lets workspace admins update settings, ask questions, and generate reports based on workspace usage and activity data.

Here’s OpenAI:

With the Admin plugin, admins can complete their day-to-day tasks directly from ChatGPT Work and Codex, including but not limited to:

Understand adoption and usage. Review activity and credit usage across ChatGPT Work and Codex, identify where additional enablement may help and when members or groups are approaching credit limits.

Manage members and groups. Add or remove members, update groups, and complete routine onboarding, offboarding, and team changes.

Manage access and permissions. Review effective permissions, diagnose access issues, and control feature or model access by role or group.

Manage usage limits and spending requests. Adjust limits for members groups, and workspaces, review requests against current usage, and approve or deny them with context.

In a demo of the new plugin, Aarti Bagul, a Member of the GTM Staff at OpenAI, shows a use case in which she is preparing for a monthly AI rollout review. title: The Fitbit Air would be S-tier if anyone made a band half as decent as Whoop’s
snippet: The Fitbit Air is being touted as a fantastic fitness tracker, but I don’t think its worth has quite yet been proven. Google-made and third-party bands do not make for a comfortable experience, and competitive trackers blow it out of the water in terms of fit.
fullText:
The Fitbit Air is being touted as a fantastic fitness tracker, but I don’t think its worth has quite yet been proven. Google-made and third-party bands do not make for a comfortable experience, and competitive trackers blow it out of the water in terms of fit.

I was a little late to jump on the Fitbit Air bandwagon. For some time, I grew accustomed to using an Oura Ring, as reviews in the past have showcased. The form factor is wonderful, and the newest model, the Oura Ring 5, gives users a more comfortable experience because it’s so much thinner. I haven’t used the newest edition, and instead walked myself back to fitness bands like the Whoop 4.0. I still had the hardware even with yet another new model available, but I find it works just fine.

It’s expensive, though.

For $25/month, you get the basics as Whoop sets them. Whoop sets them high, to be fair, just like Oura does. Elevated metrics and studies bump the price up, but Google has proven that a good health suite can be free with hardware. We’ve documented the Google Health app well, and it sets a fantastic bar for a subscription-free service. Of course, you can always opt into the AI coach powered by Gemini for an added $10/month.

	

What bothers me after using the Fitbit Air for a few weeks is the comfort, or lack thereof. Coming from Whoop’s knitted bands and clasp system, I find the Fitbit Air to be difficult to forget about. That’s what you want, after all – a band that goes unnoticed minutes after putting it on. The main point of contact should feel better than it does, and these proprietary bands just don’t do it for me.

They feel stiff, don’t seem to breathe very well, and have given me the first taste of contact dermatitis that I’ve ever experienced on a wearable. Maybe it was tighter than it needed to be, or maybe these bands don’t have any give with the natural swelling and contracting your skin does throughout the day.

The Google-made bands I’ve tried just don’t have any serviceable stretch. Granted, I haven’t used the more expensive Elevated or Active band because of the added cost at around $50. Just the Special Edition Stephen Curry band and the default Performance Loop band have lived on my pebble. Still, compared to the included strap that comes with Whoop’s fitness trackers, Google’s hardware severely lags behind.

I’d love to have a band option with a similar clasp system – something set-and-forget. By comparison, the Fitbit Air Performance Loop band requires a bit too much patience for something I need to remove and put back on daily.

The market is already flooded with Fitbit Air adapters that let you use the hardware with Whoop’s bands, but that’s literally just a band-aid. It completely negates the reason the Air exists – minimal footprint on an 18mm strap. On size alone, the Fitbit Air beats Whoop hands down.

You could make the overarching argument that the Fitbit Air’s affordable price is made possible because the sensor’s enclosure isn’t made from more premium materials, like aluminum or titanium – the latter might be overkill. That feels more like an excuse, since even additional band options don’t seem to be as premium.

The third-party landscape doesn’t offer much better than Google does, yet.

Your best bet is finding Fitbit Air bands from Amazon and even dropshipping websites like Aliexpress. Google’s good-faith move to make Fitbit Air band designs available ‘s enclosure design available hasn’t yet paid off. I haven’t found many creative or premium designs hit online stores, and if there are shops selling Fitbit Air bands, they’re generally getting them from Aliexpress.

Hopefully, that changes and we begin to see premium bands with unique hardware from accessory companies with solid track records – looking at you, UAG, Nomad, and Spigen. Those are just a couple of companies to call out, but the option is there for an accessories brand to develop some good options.

All that’s to say the Google Fitbit Air is a solid fitness tracker with an affordable price, but it would be S-tier with more comfortable bands.

title: WhatsApp announces three ways to make accounts more secure
snippet: Meta today announced a set of new security features for WhatsApp, including expanded passkey support and stronger two-step verification. Here are the details.
fullText:
Meta today announced a set of new security features for WhatsApp, including expanded passkey support and stronger two-step verification. Here are the details.

WhatsApp announces account security features

Meta today announced that WhatsApp now supports more than one passkey for the same account, a welcome feature for users who use both iOS and Android devices.

WhatsApp says more than 1 billion people now use passkeys to log back into their accounts with Face ID, Touch ID, or a screen lock code. The company first introduced passkey support on Android in October 2023 and expanded it to iPhone the following April.

Additionally, WhatsApp announced today that its two-step verification feature is expanding beyond a six-digit PIN to support full alphanumeric passwords, including special characters.

As WhatsApp explains, “two-step verification is an extra protection layer that helps prevent someone from taking over your account, even if they get hold of your one-time passcode,” and you can learn more about that here.

Finally, alas, this last feature is only available on Android for now, WhatsApp is adding a feature designed to make calls from unknown contacts safer to pick up.

From the press release:

When you get a call from someone not saved in your contacts, a little context can help you decide whether to pick up. On Android, you’ll now see more information about a non-contact caller, like whether the number is from a different country and if you have any groups in common. Scammers rely on urgency – now you can take a beat with some more info before answering.

It is worth mentioning that iPhone users can rely on a similar feature for traditional phone calls. Apple’s Call Screening feature, available on iPhones running iOS 26, automatically asks unknown callers for their name and reason for calling before the iPhone rings. Although it does not work with WhatsApp calls, you can learn more about it here.

title: Three new Macs are launching this fall, here’s what’s coming
snippet: Apple launched two new products today—Mac mini and Mac Studio—but three more Macs are rumored to arrive this fall. Here’s what’s coming.
fullText:
Apple launched two new products today—Mac mini and Mac Studio—but three more Macs are rumored to arrive this fall. Here’s what’s coming.

M6 MacBook Pro

Apple’s base model 14-inch MacBook Pro is reportedly getting an M6 update this fall. It’s expected to launch in October, right about one year after last year’s M5 model debuted.

The new MacBook Pro will have the same design as the current model. Externally, there will be little to no discernible difference. Internally though, the M6 chip that was just unveiled today will enable big performance and efficiency gains. 

M6 is built with a state-of-the-art 2-nanometer process and has “a larger 12-core CPU complex with the world’s fastest CPU core, a larger 12-core GPU with Neural Accelerators, a Dual 16-core Neural Engine, and up to 170GB/s of unified memory bandwidth.”

MacBook Pro / MacBook Ultra: New design, touchscreen, more

Apple has a new high-end MacBook coming soon that might be branded MacBook Pro or possibly MacBook Ultra. It will be powered by M5 Pro and M5 Max.

The new MacBook will offer several innovations not seen in the Mac before, including a touchscreen, OLED, Dynamic Island, and more. It will also have a brand new industrial design that’s thinner and lighter than the current MacBook Pro.

We’re expecting a launch in October, but the release could potentially slip into early 2027 instead.

M6 iMac

The iMac was originally expected to get an M5 update, but Apple is now reportedly planning to jump straight to the M6 instead.

Mark Gurman writes at Bloomberg:

Apple is preparing a version with the M6 chip that won’t change much else (other than some new color options). Nevertheless, if you’ve been holding out for a new iMac, your wait shouldn’t be much longer. All signs point to the M6 models being close to launch, and you should be able to buy one before the end of the year.

Like the new Mac mini, which also skipped M5, the M6 iMac should offer “up to 4x faster AI performance, 2x faster storage and graphics, and 40 percent faster CPU performance” compared to the previous M4 model.

title: This new Android & iPhone tracker hides in your bike or golf clubs with 3-year battery life [Gallery]
snippet: Pebblebee has launched “LÔC8,” a unique new Android Find Hub / Apple Find My tracker that’s designed to hide within your bike handles, golf clubs, and other places to help you keep tabs on your gear.
fullText:
Pebblebee has launched “LÔC8,” a unique new Android Find Hub / Apple Find My tracker that’s designed to hide within your bike handles, golf clubs, and other places to help you keep tabs on your gear.

Available alongside the company’s host of other tracker form factors, Pebblebee “LÔC8” is tailor-made to fit in places you wouldn’t expect. The cylindrical tracker’s primary targets are bikes and golf clubs, but you can technically fit it in any “shaft-like” object. But it’s definitely designed to fit into an object rather than stand on its own.

“LÔC8” has a clear plastic shell that’s not designed to be exterior-facing. But, technically, it would function if you just threw it into a backpack or suitcase pocket. Probably pretty well, too, seeing as Pebblebee touts 3-year battery life and “uncompromised performance.” At least, as long as the battery stays in place, seeing as it’s exposed in the tube.

That battery isn’t rechargeable, but it is replaceable. At least, that’s what Pebblebee says. The ER10250 cell inside, at least from my brief research, seems very hard to purchase online, so this won’t be as simple of a replacement as swapping out a coin cell. 

	

But the overall process of using this is pretty easy – certainly a lot easier than removing the grip from my bike handle (WD-40 solves all, if you’re curious).

The top of the tracker acts as a button, with a double-press activating pairing mode. From there, just connect via Android Find Hub (or iPhone Find My) on your nearby phone, insert the tracker in your bike or club or wherever you’re putting it and you’re done. There are two sleeves in the box to fit inside of bike handles of different sizes, though mainly for mountain bikes at this point. You can then slide your normal grip over the tracker. The battery goes on for three years and, if the tip of the tracker is still visible, you can see an LED light up when you locate it in the Find Hub app.

It’s a remarkably simple idea, but one that has the potential to be super useful. Bike thefts in cities are very common and, while it’s easy enough to add an AirTag-style tracker, something like this would be nearly impossible for a thief to remove. Meanwhile, for a golf club, there’s no option besides this. And it’s nice to see such an elegant solution come to reality. Pebblebee first told us about this initiative back in early 2025, and there are more ideas on the table including a “plate” style tracker that could be embedded in something like a pair of skis.

Pebblebee sells “LÔC8” in 1-pack and 4-pack options, the former costing $39.99 and being designed mainly for individual users as a DIY addition to existing gear. The 4-pack is specifically designed for golf club sets and to be installed by a professional.

fullText:
Apple has officially launched ads in Apple Maps, with the rollout ramping up in the coming weeks. Here are the details.

Ads in Apple Maps are officially rolling out now in US and Canada

There are two places you’ll find ads in the Maps app:

Before searching: Suggested Places in the search screen will feature an ad.

After searching: Ads will appear in search results when relevant.

Ads appear just like every other business listing, except they have a small blue badge that says ‘Ad.’ You can see examples of ads in the images above.

	

Like Apple’s ads policy with other services, the company touts user privacy protections for ads in Maps. Per Apple Newsroom:

Ads on Maps builds on Apple’s broader privacy-first approach to advertising, and maintains the same privacy protections Maps users enjoy today. A user’s location and the ads they see and interact with in Maps are not associated with a user’s Apple Account. Personal data stays on a user’s device, is not collected or stored by Apple, and is not shared with third parties.

title: Pixel’s ‘Flip to Shhh’ notification feature is broken for some
snippet: With the Pixel’s “Flip to Shhh” feature on, setting the phone face down silences notifications. It’s a handy feature for disconnecting, but it’s not actually working on several models right now.
fullText:
With the Pixel’s “Flip to Shhh” feature on, setting the phone face down silences notifications. It’s a handy feature for disconnecting, but it’s not actually working on several models right now.

Several device models from the Pixel 7 to the Pixel 10 seem to have an issue with Flip to Shhh. Users have started reporting that the setting is simply unavailable after one change or another.

Stories vary from user to user, with one noting they simply turned on Advanced Protection and switched launcher preferences before the feature disappeared, while another said they turned it off by accident. One even said the issue began happening after they reset their Pixel 10 Pro XL.

Across the board, though, enabling it again surfaces a “can’t turn on flip to shhh” error. It seems to be a server-side issue with conflicting Digital Wellbeing versions. For a few users, forcing the Digital Wellbeing app to update in the Google Play Store resets Flip to Shhh, and it can then be enabled again.

	

Granted, the recent posts that have begun making the rounds are weeks old at this point, but updates to the original complaints prove a fix still hasn’t been found. Since updating Digital Wellbeing, it looks like some have seen the issue reappear, with no way to turn the notification setting on again.

Ironically, this bug crops up after Google launches the Pixel 11 series with a similar feature – HiLight. It works in conjunction with Flip to Shhh to enhance notifications without disruption, but it’s unlikely that Digital Wellbeing is broken due to new hardware in the pipeline.

It’s unclear why the Digital Wellbeing service is disrupting the feature with passing updates. For now, there doesn’t seem to be a definitive fix for affected devices.

title: Apple just revealed two ways iPhone 18 Pro could get big upgrades
snippet: Today Apple unveiled its M6 chip, the first of a new chip generation that will soon include iPhone 18 Pro’s A20 Pro. Here’s what the M6 reveals about iPhone 18 Pro gains to expect.
fullText:
Today Apple unveiled its M6 chip, the first of a new chip generation that will soon include iPhone 18 Pro’s A20 Pro. Here’s what the M6 reveals about iPhone 18 Pro gains to expect.

M6 points to iPhone 18 Pro having big performance and efficiency gains with A20 Pro

It’s not September yet, but Apple launched two surprise products today: a new Mac mini and Mac Studio. (Pre-orders available now: Mac mini, Mac Studio.)

The Mac mini comes with Apple’s next-generation M6 chip, which belongs to the same family of chips as iPhone 18 Pro’s upcoming A20 Pro.

Here’s how Apple introduced it, per Apple Newsroom:

M6 is built using cutting-edge 2 nm process technology, packing greater transistor density into a smaller die for a major leap in performance and power efficiency. M6 also introduces a Dual 16-core Neural Engine, providing up to 2x the peak compute over previous generations to make on-device AI workflows run even faster. […]

M6 has a brand-new 12-core CPU complex — two more cores than M5 — that consists of 2 super cores, 4 performance cores, and 6 efficiency cores. It delivers the world’s fastest single-threaded performance and up to 1.2x faster multithreaded performance as compared to M5

M6 will ultimately prove more powerful than the iPhone 18 Pro‘s new A20 Pro chip. That’s true of Mac and iPad-class M chips in general.

But because M6 and A20 Pro are part of the same family of chips, the upgrades announced for M6 are expected to reflect changes coming in A20 Pro too.

And most notably, A20 Pro will use the new 2-nanometer process Apple highlights as enabling “a major leap in performance and power efficiency” with M6.

We’ve suspected that the transition to 2nm will bring bigger than usual gains. But the M6 details confirm that.

A20 Pro may not have the same number of CPU and GPU cores as M6. And the Dual 16-core Neural Engine is a question mark too. But thanks to 2-nanometer technology, it should bring big improvements in the two areas Apple highlighted today: performance and efficiency.

What will the exact year-over-year improvements be? It’s hard to say for sure. But when iPhone 18 Pro is unveiled in a couple of weeks, expect to see performance and efficiency be key upgrades of the A20 Pro.

title: Google Home bug reportedly breaks Keep’s shopping list integration
snippet: Users are finding that Google Home’s longstanding skill of adding items to shopping lists with voice commands has disintegrated, but it all seems to be part of a strange bug for a number of people.
fullText:
Users are finding that Google Home’s longstanding skill of adding items to shopping lists with voice commands has disintegrated, but it all seems to be part of a strange bug for a number of people.

As Google has begun rolling out Gemini for Home to users, bugs with voice commands and the Home app have begun appearing more frequently, or so it seems. The latest breaks the link between Google Assistant or Gemini’s and its ability to add items to a shopping list in Google Keep.

Users are noting on Reddit that asking the usual “add [items] to my [list name] list” isn’t working anymore (via Android Authority). Instead of adding entries to a saved list in the user’s Google Keep notes, the assistant will give information unrelated to the shopping list, or fail to load entirely.

What should happen is that Gemini for Google Home adds the items to the shopping list without an issue. But there’s a break in the usual process, leading to confusion among some users. One user reports that Google Home’s assistant would repeat the same question.

	

The issue isn’t fully widespread and seems to be affecting a chunk of users while being a non-issue for others. Some have found that the notes and lists setting in Google Home is disabled entirely, with no way to turn it back on. That could be preventing Gemini from accessing Google Keep lists and making edits.

On our end, asking Gemini to create a new list and add items to it was a flawless process. That isn’t to say we don’t experience frustrating hiccups more often than we’d like. Still, this particular issue isn’t happening here, but that clearly isn’t the case for everyone.

Google has not seemingly addressed the issue, though Google Home updates have been frequent and have addressed some previous bugs rather quickly.

title: Nothing’s Android 17 update debuts this week with redesigns, new apps, 3D emoji [Gallery]
snippet: Nothing has announced Nothing OS 5.0, its Android 17 update, which will start rolling out in October with some redesigned UI elements, more AI features, new apps, and support for Google’s 3D emoji too.
fullText:
Nothing has announced Nothing OS 5.0, its Android 17 update, which will start rolling out in October with some redesigned UI elements, more AI features, new apps, and support for Google’s 3D emoji too.

Nothing OS 5.0 isn’t a complete overhaul, but it’s not a small update either. Rolling out starting in October, the Android 17-based update brings a host of new updates throughout. This includes various UI updates, including Pixel-like transparency/blur on some homescreen widgets and in apps like Nothing Gallery, lockscreen clock faces, batch editing on the homescreen, new widgets, and even a new dedicated app for Nothing’s Glyph features.

A condensed version of the changelog for Nothing OS 5.0 follows:

New font throughout the system UI

Status bar animations for feedback when changing connection modes, more

Camera app: Updated icons, QR links now stay fixed on screen once recognized

Nothing Gallery gets better sorting, album organization options

New homescreen personalization and batch editing

Lockscreen gets two new clocks and more color theming

Wallpapers add more depth and blur effects

New widgets: “Away Time” to show time not using your phone, “Collector” for sticker-like widgets on homescreen created from photos

Dedicated Glyph app for light controls, features, etc

Bluetooth controls upgraded in Quick Settings

Essential AI updates:

Essential Voice now shows a live preview of text while processing voice-to-text output

“Smart Collections” automatically sort Essential Space content

Essential Apps can now be built through an app on your Nothing Phone

Separate Quick Settings & Notification panels (optional)

Yellow AI privacy indicator

Noto 3D emoji (also available on Pixel 11)

Nothing says to expect Nothing OS 5.0 (Android 17) to start rolling out to Phone (3) in “mid-October,” with the rest of its supported devices – dating back to Phone (2a) – being updated through mid-January. 

	

Open Beta builds will be available starting tomorrow, August 26, starting on Phone (3) and expanding to other devices in the coming weeks. Somewhat amusingly, Phone (4b) is second-to-last in line, despite being the company’s newest smartphone.

snippet: Apple TV has a new original comedy series—Brothers—coming next month with Matthew McConaughey and Woody Harrelson. Here’s the trailer.
fullText:
Apple TV has a new original comedy series—Brothers—coming next month with Matthew McConaughey and Woody Harrelson. Here’s the trailer.

‘Brothers’ comedy series coming September 23 from The Office’s Lee Eisenberg

Apple TV is currently airing Ted Lasso season 4, but another high-profile comedy is coming soon.

Matthew McConaughey and Woody Harrelson star in Brothers, a new original series where they play fictionalized versions of themselves.

Brothers premieres Wednesday, September 23 with two episodes, followed by weekly releases through November 4.

The showrunner is Lee Eisenberg, who was a significant creative player on the beloved sitcom The Office. Eisenberg was a writer and producer on the series for seasons 2 through 6.

Here’s Apple’s plot summary for Brothers, followed by the trailer:

“Brothers” follows McConaughey and Harrelson, who play fictionalized versions of themselves, and whose friendship is thrown into chaos when they uncover a decades-old secret: they might actually be brothers. After Woody’s daughter’s engagement falls apart, he loads up the family and heads to Austin for an extended stay at Matthew’s ranch. But what begins as a healing getaway quickly spirals when Matthew’s mother, Ma Mac (played by Holland Taylor), accidentally lets slip a long-buried secret that the two friends might actually be brothers. As Woody turns the ranch upside down in pursuit of the truth, Matthew finds himself juggling an entirely different identity crisis: a potential run for governor of Texas. The result is a heartfelt, chaotic and wildly funny story about friendship, family, fame and the messy line between myth and reality.

Also coming to Apple TV in September alongside Brothers: a new season of Slow Horses, an original crime thriller called Last Seen, and the Ryan Reynolds film Mayday.

title: M6 Mac mini vs M4 Mac mini: Here are all the new features
snippet: Today Apple launched a new Mac mini, available in M6 and M5 Pro configurations. Here’s everything new compared to the M4 and M4 Pro Mac mini models.
fullText:
Today Apple launched a new Mac mini, available in M6 and M5 Pro configurations. Here’s everything new compared to the M4 and M4 Pro Mac mini models.

Chips: M6 and M5 Pro vs M4 and M4 Pro

The new Mac mini is all about improved performance. Both models include a “newly optimized thermal design,” but beyond that, each chip differs significantly. Whether you choose the M6 or M5 Pro though, you’ll get big upgrades.

M6 vs M4

M6 is Apple’s newest chip and the first built on an innovative 2nm process. That means it packs larger than usual improvements. For example, M6 has up to 2x faster storage than M4.

M6 features a 12-core CPU and 12-core GPU, up from 10 cores each in M4. The extra CPU cores are 2 “super cores.”

M6 also packs a dual 16-core Neural Engine, doubling the number of Neural Engine cores for huge AI-related gains.

In summary, Apple says this all translates to “up to 4x faster AI performance, 2x faster storage and graphics, and 40 percent faster CPU performance.”

M5 Pro vs M4 Pro

M5 Pro offers a 15-core CPU (up from 12) that’s configurable up to 18 cores with 6 super cores and 12 performance cores. It also offers an up to 20-core GPU.

Here are some stats from Apple on what these upgrades look like in use:

Up to 4x faster LLM prompt processing performance in LM Studio compared to M4 Pro

Up to 1.4x faster rendering performance with ray tracing in Blender compared to M4 Pro

Up to 1.5x faster image processing in Affinity compared to M4 Pro

Memory upgrades

Memory upgrades in the new Mac mini give you higher memory bandwidth and a higher ceiling for RAM configurations—at least compared to what has recently been available.

Mac mini with M6 offers memory bandwidth up to 170GB/s vs 120GB/s on the M4. With M5 Pro you get 307GB/s memory bandwidth, up from 273GB/s with M4 Pro.

M6 Mac mini is configurable with up to 32GB of RAM, while M4 was only available with a max of 24GB. M5 Pro Mac mini offers up to 64GB of RAM, up from the 48GB available in M4 Pro.

Note: M4 models used to offer comparable max RAM configurations, but those high-end options were removed earlier this year.

Connectivity

Apple has several improvements for connectivity in the new Mac mini.

Its N1 wireless chip that debuted in iPhone 17 is a new addition, which offers two upgrades:

Wi-Fi 7, up from Wi-Fi 6E

Bluetooth 6, up from Bluetooth 5.3

2.5Gb Ethernet is now standard in Mac mini, and there’s an optional 10Gb option. Previously, you could only choose from Gigabit or 10Gb.

Genlock support through USB-C is another new connectivity feature. It lets you achieve precise synchronization between a display and camera, including iPhone 17 Pro.

M6 and M5 Pro Mac mini: Pricing and availability

Mac mini with M6 has an $899 starting price, up from $799 for the M4 model. This is also significantly higher than the $599 starting price the M4 Mac mini launched at in 2024.

Mac mini with M5 Pro starts at $1,699, up from the $1,599 latest starting price of M4 Pro.

The new Mac mini is available to pre-order now, and ships starting September 22.

title: Galaxy S27 Ultra’s major redesign detailed in new renders, price hike rumored
snippet: Samsung’s new Galaxy S27 Ultra is getting a massive redesign and, thanks to the latest leak, we’ve got a better look at what to expect, but we’re also now bracing for a major price hike.
fullText:
Samsung’s new Galaxy S27 Ultra is getting a massive redesign and, thanks to the latest leak, we’ve got a better look at what to expect, but we’re also now bracing for a major price hike.

Following leaks over the weekend that first depicted Samsung’s new design, @OnLeaks and Android Headlines have posted CAD-based renders of the Galaxy S27 Ultra’s new design. While these renders are never completely infallible – mistakes have been made before – the track record speaks for itself, and it’s very likely this is the device we’ll see released in January.

With that in mind, this is a pretty radical redesign on Samsung’s part, especially just months after the company insisted its vertical camera design was its “core identity.”

The new look has a camera plateau similar to the iPhone 16 series, while the overall shape of the device is mostly unchanged. It is a little bit bigger, though, with the dimensions supposedly coming in at 163.76 x 78.25 x 7.97mm – just a hair larger in every dimension compared to Galaxy S26 Ultra. The camera module bumps out to 12.53mm, apparently, which sounds wild. 

	

The S Pen also remains in place here.

Galaxy S27 Ultra is expected to be a pretty big upgrade, also packing a much larger battery, Qualcomm’s new Snapdragon flagship, and more, though it is losing a telephoto camera.

That might all come at a cost, though. A post on Twitter/X from @phonefuturist claims that Galaxy S27 Ultra could start at a whopping $1,499 – a $200 price hike over the current S26 Ultra. And, despite the new design, Qi2 magnets still won’t be included. That said, we’re taking this claim with a huge grain of salt, as we’re not sure of the track record of this account. Neither claim is unreasonable, though.

title: Apple outlines 50 ways to make devices easier to use as we age
snippet: Apple hit its 50th birthday this year, and many of its customers are even older. The company has created a new support page outlining 50 ways to make its devices easier to use, mostly using accessibility settings. These range from changing the size of text on an Apple Watch to having your iPhone alert you when your washing machine cycle is complete …
fullText:
Apple hit its 50th birthday this year, and many of its customers are even older. The company has created a new support page outlining 50 ways to make its devices easier to use, mostly using accessibility settings.

These range from changing the size of text on an Apple Watch to having your iPhone alert you when your washing machine cycle is complete …

Apple says that it aims to make its technology accessible to everyone, including older adults.

At Apple, we believe the best technology works for everyone, including older adults. That’s why our products and services are inclusive by design, with built-in accessibility features to help you connect, create, and do what you love—in the ways that work best for you.

As life changes, so do the ways we want to interact with the world around us. From making text larger onscreen to adding clarity to a conversation in a busy restaurant, Apple’s ecosystem of devices, features, and services is built to adapt to meet your needs.

The support page mostly points to accessibility features, divided into ten categories.

Vision: View what’s on screen more comfortably

Hearing: Connect with conversations, alerts, and your environment

Mobility: Adapt how you navigate and control your device

Speech: Your voice, your way

Cognitive: Find your focus and feel in control

Personalization: Make it yours

Organization: Remember what matters

Health: Your health, through helpful insights

Safety: For peace of mind

Communication: Stay connected

The vision category, for example, includes increasing text size, making fonts bold, inverting colours, setting up colour filters, reducing transparency, increasing contrast, and reducing flicker. Some, like sound recognition, are not widely known despite Apple highlighting them at the time of launch.

Sound Recognition listens for certain sounds and uses on‑device intelligence to notify you when they are detected. This feature recognizes 15 different sounds — or you can train your device to listen for your name, as well as electronic sounds that are unique to your environment, like the beeping of appliances in your kitchen, specific types of alarms, or doorbells. On HomePod, Sound Recognition can also detect the sound of a smoke or carbon monoxide alarm.

Sound Recognition supports CarPlay, too. Your iPhone will listen for and detect sirens and horns and even the sound of a crying baby. You’ll receive a notification — onscreen in your car if you’re using CarPlay — when a particular sound is detected.

The page is an impressive encapsulation of just how many accessibility features are now available across Apple devices. Each subsection has separate instructions for each supported device. Depending on the feature, this may span iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple Watch, Apple TV, Vision Pro, and CarPlay.

title: WhatsApp two-step verification codes are ditching six-digit PINs for full passwords
snippet: WhatsApp is making some security upgrades, including turning two-step verification codes into full passwords instead of the traditional six-digit numerical PIN.
fullText:
WhatsApp is making some security upgrades, including turning two-step verification codes into full passwords instead of the traditional six-digit numerical PIN.

Alongside celebrating that one billion of its users are now using passkeys, WhatsApp has two new account security features rolling out.

The first is an upgrade to two-step verification codes used with WhatsApp. 

No longer are these codes just a six-digit numerical PIN, but a full password. WhatsApp says these will be “longer, alphanumeric,” and include special characters (@,$, etc) to make the password harder to guess. w

	

Two-step verification is getting stronger: Two-step verification is an extra protection layer that helps prevent someone from taking over your account, even if they get hold of your one-time passcode. Until now it was a six-digit PIN, we’ve now upgraded it to a full password: longer, alphanumeric, and even with special ch@racters to make it harder to guess. If you’ve been using “123456,” this is your sign to upgrade.

On Android, WhatsApp is also rolling out a new screen for calls that are coming from unknown callers, with the incoming call screen now showing context such as country of origin and whether or not the number is in any of the groups you’re in.

title: Wyze’s new Indoor Cam Pan has 360-degree tracking and built-in privacy for under $40
snippet: Wyze is refreshing its 360-degree Indoor Cam Pan with an improved design and better night vision, and a price of just $40.
fullText:
Wyze is refreshing its 360-degree Indoor Cam Pan with an improved design and better night vision, and a price of just $40.

Available starting today, the Wyze Indoor Cam Pan is a camera on a motorized base, allowing it to swivel 360-degrees around. The lens itself is mounted on a second vertical motor that can move 103-degrees up or down. In other words, it can see basically everywhere around where you put it.

title: Qualcomm’s next Snapdragon flagship chip has 5 GHz Oryon CPU
snippet: Ahead of Snapdragon Summit 2026 next month, Qualcomm is previewing three components of its “next-generation Snapdragon flagship platform” (chip), starting with the Oryon CPU today.
fullText:
Ahead of Snapdragon Summit 2026 next month, Qualcomm is previewing three components of its “next-generation Snapdragon flagship platform” (chip), starting with the Oryon CPU today.

The upcoming Snapdragon chip will feature a new Oryon CPU that “is the first mobile CPU to reach 5 GHz.” For reference, the 8 Elite Gen 5 reached 4.74 GHz and the 8 Elite before it was at 4.47 GHz.

Qualcomm credits a “fully custom design” from the microarchitecture to the CPU subsystem and “implementation choices behind it” as making this possible. This clock speed “doesn’t come from a process node alone.” A diagram shared today shows two Prime Cores and six Performance Cores. 

That speed is paired with exceptional instructions per clock, or IPC, so the performance shows up in real-world use cases.

Exact specs or the name aren’t being shared today, but there is:

	

A “large L1 instruction cache in each core keeps the CPU from wasting cycles.”

An “L2 cache sits directly in the CPU complex to keep this large pool right next to the cores.”

Meanwhile, the “Qualcomm Oryon FlexCache” architecture allows “heterogeneous cores to access the same cache pool, with cache dynamically allocated based on workload.” If required by a workload, the Prime Cores “can draw on the entire pool.”

Larger working sets stay resident instead of spilling to memory, so peak performance holds instead of tapering off the moment a task outgrows its share.

In recognition of the industry’s ongoing “memory constraints,” Qualcomm says “FlexCache reduces how often the cores need to reach system memory, so performance holds up even when memory is limited.” In terms of real-world performance, this translates to:

Agentic AI. An agent doesn’t do one task; it manages a chain of them, and the steps hand off between cores. Every core works from the same place, so the dataset stays resident as tasks hand off, and agents migrate between cores.

Gaming. Optimized access to local cache boosts performance and stabilizes frame rates, reducing dropped frames and stutter.

Multitasking. Switching between apps moves work from one core to another. A shared cache means that handoff doesn’t start cold, so returning to what you were doing picks up quickly.

Video editing. Decode, effects, and export hand frames from one stage to the next, often across different cores. Those handoffs stay inside the cache instead of routing through the interconnect.

Snapdragon Summit takes place September 22-24, with Qualcomm previewing the upcoming chip’s GPU and NPU in the coming weeks.

title: Apple unveils new Mac Studio with M5 Max and M5 Ultra
snippet: Alongside the new Mac mini, Apple today has announced its next-generation Mac Studio. The new Mac Studio lineup is powered by the M5 Max and M5 Ultra chips and supports up to 512GB of unified memory. The new Mac Studio models are available to pre-order today.
fullText:
Alongside the new Mac mini, Apple today has announced its next-generation Mac Studio. The new Mac Studio lineup is powered by the M5 Max and M5 Ultra chips and supports up to 512GB of unified memory.

The new Mac Studio models are available to pre-order today. 

M5 Max Mac Studio

First, Apple has announced a new Mac Studio powered by M5 Max, an upgrade from the previous-generation M4 Max model. The M5 Max first debuted in the MacBook Pro earlier this year.

M5 Max features an 18-core CPU with 6 super cores and 12 performance cores. The GPU can be configured with up to 40 cores, with Neural Accelerators built into each core. Apple says GPU performance is up to 50% faster than the previous generation. It offers up to 614GB/s of unified memory bandwidth, up from up to 546 GB/s with the M4 Max generation.

The M5 Max Mac Studio starts with 36GB of unified memory and supports up to 128GB. For comparison’s sake, those numbers are the same as when the M4 Max Mac Studio was first announced. In the intervening year, however, Apple has gradually whittled down the options due to the industry-wide memory shortage. As of yesterday, the M4 Max Mac Studio started at 36GB of memory and maxed out at 96GB.

Here are some benchmarks Apple shared for the M5 Max Mac Studio:

Up to 10.7x faster LLM prompt processing in LM Studio when compared to Mac Studio with M1 Max, and 3.9x faster than M4 Max.

Up to 7.4x faster text-to-image performance when compared to Mac Studio with M1 Max, and up to 3.5x faster than M4 Max.

Up to 5.3x faster Magic Mask performance in Blackmagic Design DaVinci Resolve Studio when compared to Mac Studio with M1 Max, and up to 3x faster than M4 Max.

Up to 3.5x faster basecalling for DNA sequencing in Oxford Nanopore MinKNOW when compared to Mac Studio with M1 Max, and up to 1.9x faster than M4 Max

M5 Ultra Mac Studio

The real star of the show today is the M5 Ultra Mac Studio.

The new M5 Ultra Mac Studio offers up to a 36-core CPU with 12 super cores and 24 performance cores. This delivers up to 1.3x higher multithreaded performance than the previous-generation M3 Ultra Mac Studio.

The M5 Ultra packs an up-to-80-core GPU, which Apple says is the most powerful Apple silicon GPU ever. This also marks the first time Apple has added its Neural Accelerators to the Ultra chip. Neural Accelerators are dedicated hardware in each GPU core designed to speed up AI workloads.

In terms of memory, Mac Studio with M5 Ultra starts with 96GB and can be configured with up to 512GB. This is unchanged from when the M3 Ultra Mac Studio first launched. Over the last year, however, Apple cut the M3 Ultra Mac Studio memory options to just 96GB due to memory shortages. Memory bandwidth clocks in at up to 1.2TB/s.

The M5 Ultra’s Media Engine has twice the video encode and decode blocks as M5 Max, supporting up to 33 simultaneous streams of 8K ProRes video.

Apple touts the following benchmarks for the M5 Ultra Mac Studio:

Up to 15.4x faster CopyCat ML training performance in Foundry Nuke when compared to Mac Studio with M1 Ultra, and up to 3.3x faster than M3 Ultra.

Up to 9.8x faster LLM prompt processing in LM Studio when compared to Mac Studio with M1 Ultra, and up to 4x faster than M3 Ultra.

Up to 8.2x faster text-to-image performance when compared to Mac Studio with M1 Ultra, and up to 4.3x faster than M3 Ultra.

Up to 4.7x faster scene rendering performance in Maxon Redshift when compared to Mac Studio with M1 Ultra, and up to 1.7x faster than M3 Ultra.

More Mac Studio specs and tidbits

Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6, powered by Apple’s N1 networking chip

Support for up to eight external displays, or up to four Studio Display XDR at 5K resolution and 120Hz refresh rate

Storage performance is up to twice as fast thanks to PCIe Gen 6 support

Thunderbolt 5 with up to 120Gb/s bandwidth

Support for genlock over USB-C for precise synchronization between a display and professional camera capture.

Mac Studio pricing and availability

Mac Studio with M5 Max starts at $2,499, and the base configuration includes 512GB of storage. That price is unchanged compared to the M4 Max Mac Studio. Mac Studio with M5 Ultra starts at $5,499 with 1TB of storage. That is a $200 increase compared to the M3 Ultra configuration.

The new Mac Studio lineup is available to order starting today and will begin arriving to customers on September 22. Apple, however, says the M5 Ultra Mac Studio with 512GB of memory “is coming in late October.”

title: Apple launches next-gen Apple Silicon chips: M6 and M5 Ultra
snippet: Apple has unveiled two new Apple Silicon chips today. The M6 chip debuts in a new Mac mini model and marks Apple’s first 2nm processor. The M5 Ultra launches in a refreshed Mac Studio and is Apple’s most powerful chip ever.
fullText:
Apple has unveiled two new Apple Silicon chips today. The M6 chip debuts in a new Mac mini model and marks Apple’s first 2nm processor. The M5 Ultra launches in a refreshed Mac Studio and is Apple’s most powerful chip ever.

Apple’s new M6 chip

The M6 is Apple’s first 2-nanometer chip, which the company says increases transistor density and power efficiency. This allows it to upgrade compute blocks without increasing die size.

The M6 features a 12-core CPU, two more than the M5 chip. Notably, it’s Apple’s first processor with all three CPU core types. That includes two super cores, four performance cores, and six efficiency cores.

Super cores prioritize maximum single-threaded performance and are Apple’s most powerful core type. Performance cores are optimized for demanding multithreaded work, and efficiency cores handle background tasks.

All told, Apple says this means M6 has “the world’s fastest single-threaded performance” and offers “up to 1.2x faster multithreaded performance as compared to M5.”

M6 features a 12-core GPU, which is two more cores than M5. There’s a Neural Accelerator in each core. Apple says this enables a 30% increase in peak GPU compute for AI compared to M5. The M6 GPU also features updates to its shader core architecture, Dynamic Caching, and hardware-accelerated ray tracing.

M6 supports up to 32GB of unified memory with up to 170GB/s of unified memory bandwidth. That’s up to 10% faster than M5.

Additionally, M6 can process FP8 natively in hardware, whereas M5 handles FP8 through software. FP8 is an 8-bit format designed to make AI workloads faster and more memory-efficient

M6 specs and benchmarks:

CPU: Up to 1.2x faster multithreaded performance than M5 and 2.4x faster than M1.

GPU AI compute: Nearly 30% higher peak GPU compute for AI than M5 and more than 8x higher than M1.

Geometry performance: 50% higher geometry rates for complex graphics.

Neural Engine: The Dual 16-core Neural Engine delivers up to 2x the peak compute of previous generations.

Memory bandwidth: Up to 170GB/s, 10% higher than M5 and 2.5x M1.

M6 is launching today in the new Mac mini, which you can read more about in our dedicated coverage.

M5 Ultra

At the high end, Apple has announced the M5 Ultra. The company says this is its “most powerful chip ever.” The headlining change is that the M5 Ultra uses a next-generation UltraFusion technology.

Apple explains that the new UltraFusion technology connects two dual-die M5 Max chips, resulting in its first quad-die chip architecture. The new UltraFusion design delivers more than 4.4TB/s of inter-die bandwidth and over 6x higher connection density, allowing all four dies to behave as a single unified processor.

M5 Ultra offers an up-to-36-core CPU with 12 super cores and 24 performance cores. Apple says this enables up to 1.25x higher single-threaded performance and up to 1.3x higher multithreaded performance compared to M3 Ultra.

For graphics, the M5 Ultra offers a next-generation GPU with up to 80 cores, with a Neural Accelerator in each core. Apple says M5 Ultra offers up to 4.5x peak GPU compute for AI compared to M3 Ultra.

More M5 Ultra GPU specs include:

Apple’s latest shader core with second-generation dynamic caching

Hardware-accelerated mesh shading

Third-generation ray tracing

All in all, Apple says you can expect up to 40% faster graphics performance with M5 Ultra compared to M3 Ultra.

M5 Ultra supports up to 512GB of unified memory with up to 1.2TB/s of unified memory bandwidth, which is 50% higher than M3 Ultra. 

M5 Ultra specs and benchmarks

CPU: Up to 1.25x faster single-threaded performance and 1.3x faster multithreaded performance than M3 Ultra. 

GPU AI compute: Up to 4.5x the peak GPU compute for AI compared to M3 Ultra and over 6x compared to M1 Ultra. 

Graphics: Up to 40% faster graphics performance than M3 Ultra. 

Memory bandwidth: 1.2TB/s, which is 50% higher than M3 Ultra.

M5 Ultra is launching today in the new Mac Studio, which you can learn more about in our full coverage.

title: Apple announces updated Mac mini, here’s everything new
snippet: Apple today announced the first Mac mini update in nearly two years. The new Mac mini keeps the same compact design, but delivers a major performance boost with the new M6 and M5 Pro configurations. The new Mac mini lineup is available to pre-order today, with the first orders arriving September 22.
fullText:
Apple today announced the first Mac mini update in nearly two years. The new Mac mini keeps the same compact design, but delivers a major performance boost with the new M6 and M5 Pro configurations. 

The new Mac mini lineup is available to pre-order today, with the first orders arriving September 22. 

M6 Mac mini

The previous generation Mac mini was powered by the M4 and M4 Pro chips. Apple has taken a different strategy this time, opting to use the all-new M6 chip for the base configuration. The next tier, meanwhile, is powered by the M5 Pro, which first debuted in the MacBook Pro earlier this year.

The M6 chip in Mac mini is Apple’s first 2nm processor. It features a 12-core CPU, which is two more cores than M4 and M5. Apple touts that it offers “the world’s fastest single-threaded performance.” 

M6 is Apple’s first chip to use all three of its CPU core types: 2 super cores, 4 performance cores, and 6 efficiency cores. Super cores prioritize maximum single-threaded performance, performance cores are optimized for multithreaded workloads, and efficiency cores handle lighter and background tasks

Apple says that combination delivers up to 40% faster multithreaded performance than M4. 

You get a 12-core GPU, which is also two more cores than before. Apple is also bringing its Neural Accelerators to the base Mac mini for the first time, resulting in up to 4x faster AI performance and 2x faster graphics than M4.

M6 also has the new dual 16-core Neural Engine, which Apple says is up to 2x faster than the previous generation. 

The M6 Mac mini starts with 16GB of unified memory and is configurable up to 32GB. It also offers faster memory bandwidth at 170GB/s, up from 153GB/s on the M5 chip and 120GB/s on the M4.

Here are some performance statistics for Mac mini with M6 shared by Apple:

Up to 13.5x faster LLM prompt processing in LM Studio when compared to Mac mini with M1, and up to 4.8x faster than M4.

Up to 2.3x faster spreadsheet calculations in Microsoft Excel when compared to Mac mini with M1, and up to 1.5x faster than M4.

Up to 2x faster gaming performance with ray tracing in Cyberpunk 2077: Ultimate Edition when compared to Mac mini with M4.

M5 Pro Mac mini

Meanwhile, the higher-specification Mac mini offers the M5 Pro chip. You can get up to an 18-core CPU paired with up to a 20-core GPU. The GPU has Neural Accelerators in every core, an enhanced shader core, and third-generation ray tracing.

The Mac mini with M5 Pro supports up to 64GB unified memory with 307GB/s bandwidth. 

Here are Apple’s benchmarks for Mac mini powered by M5 Pro: 

Up to 8.5x faster LLM prompt processing performance in LM Studio when compared to Mac mini with M2 Pro, and up to 4x faster than M4 Pro.

Up to 4.5x faster rendering performance with ray tracing in Blender when compared to Mac mini with M2 Pro, and up to 1.4x faster than M4 Pro.

Up to 2.1x faster image processing in Affinity when compared to Mac mini with M2 Pro, and up to 1.5x faster than M4 Pro.

More Mac mini specs

Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6, thanks to Apple’s N1 chip

2.5Gb Ethernet is now standard, with 10Gb available as an upgrade

Both models have storage that’s up to 2x faster

Genlock support over USB-C for precise synchronization between a display and professional camera capture.

M6 Mac mini: Three Thunderbolt 4 ports on the back, along with HDMI and Ethernet. Two USB-C ports with USB 3 support and a headphone jack on the front.

M5 Pro Mac mini: Three Thunderbolt 5 ports on the back, along with HDMI and Ethernet. Two USB-C ports with USB 3 support and a headphone jack on the front. 

New Mac mini pricing and availability

	

The new Mac mini is available for pre-order today and will start arriving for customers on September 22. Pricing starts at $899 for the base configuration with the M6 chip, 256GB of storage, and 16GB of unified memory. Mac mini with M5 Pro starts at $1,699.

title: AI awaiting its iPhone moment, says Altman; needs to learn key Apple lesson
snippet: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman says that AI is still awaiting its iPhone moment, and that he needs to learn a key lesson from Apple. He also admits that he was overly ambitious in his idea of how quickly AI would disrupt the economy, but thinks that, paradoxically, the tech will create new opportunities for businesses that don’t use it …
fullText:
OpenAI CEO Sam Altman says that AI is still awaiting its iPhone moment, and that he needs to learn a key lesson from Apple.

He also admits that he was overly ambitious in his idea of how quickly AI would disrupt the economy, but thinks that, paradoxically, the tech will create new opportunities for businesses that don’t use it … 

AI awaiting the iPhone moment

Altman made the comments in a David Senra podcast episode reported by TNW. He likened the current AI era to the smartphone days prior to the launch of the iPhone. Many of us in the tech world owned Windows CE, Nokia, and PalmOS devices from the mid-1990s, but it was the iPhone that transformed smartphones from nerdy pocket computers to mass-market devices.

Altman compared the current phase to smartphones before Apple arrived. He had a Palm Treo around 2003 […] “We have all of the technological pieces, but we have not had the iPhone moment of completely changing how someone interfaces with technology.”

He says that AI companies, including his own, haven’t yet found the magic formula to really bring the tech into everyday consumer life.

He needs to learn a key Apple lesson

Steve Jobs famously said that one of the key reasons Apple was successful was that the company didn’t try to do too much, saying “no” to a thousand good ideas in order to fully focus on the very few products where the company said “yes.”

Altman referenced this, saying he was bad at killing good ideas in order to protect the great ones.

The greatest small business boom ever

He believes one of the key changes we are going to see is “the greatest boom in people starting smaller businesses that we have ever seen.”

In part, this will be because of the things AI makes possible, but he also predicts a less obvious outcome. He says some businesses will succeed “precisely because they have nothing to do with AI; people will want authentic, non-technological experiences.”

The episode sounds well worth listening to, and I have it in my queue.

title: DuckDuckGo survey highlights how much personal information users share with AI
snippet: Private search company DuckDuckGo has released a new survey highlighting just how much personal information people are sharing with AI chatbots, and how little many understand about what happens to those conversations. Here are the details.
fullText:
Private search company DuckDuckGo has released a new survey highlighting just how much personal information people are sharing with AI chatbots, and how little many understand about what happens to those conversations. Here are the details.

Survey shows AI users are sharing more than they realize

In a survey published today, DuckDuckGo highlights several privacy-related aspects around how people use AI chatbots, including the fact that nearly one in three users have told an AI something they would not tell friends, family, colleagues, or medical professionals. Among self-described AI enthusiasts, that figure rises to 56%.

Here’s DuckDuckGo:

For many people, AI chatbots serve as a judgement-free space to share things they won’t tell anyone else. While a typical web search might be a few words, AI chat invites longer, more personal input. Search queries reveal interests, but AI conversations have the potential to reveal thought processes, communication styles, and more.

The company says that among the nearly 2,000 U.S. adults who responded to the survey, 53% did not know or were unsure that most chatbots use conversations for training by default, while just 25% knew that AI chats can be subpoenaed by law enforcement.

Once people know it’s happening, 58% of people are uncomfortable with how their conversations are being used to train AI. (30% specify “very uncomfortable.”)

The results also show a significant behavioral divide between parents and non-parents, with parents or guardians with children in the household confiding in AI almost twice as much as non-parents. DuckDuckGo says that “among parents who use AI, 43% have told an AI something they’ve never shared with another person,” while “that number drops to 25% for AI users with no children at home.”

DuckDuckGo argues that AI companies have leaned into this behavior by encouraging users to treat chatbots as confidants in advertising campaigns and media appearances, even though those conversations may not be as private as users are led to believe.

When it comes to trust, the survey found that people have slightly more confidence in large AI companies than in the U.S. government to protect their data. However, skepticism remains high toward both: 39% said they have no trust at all in large AI companies, compared with 48% who said the same of the government.

Finally, DuckDuckGo argues that users still have an opportunity to change how they approach AI privacy, particularly as chatbot habits are still relatively new:

When we talk about online privacy in search engines and browsers, many people think “it’s too late, my information is already out there.” But the most valuable information you could share with Big Tech is your next question, not the questions you asked days or months or years ago. So, it’s never too late to make the switch to more private services online.

The company also reminds users that they can take proactive steps to protect their privacy when using AI chatbots, including choosing services with clearer and more transparent data-handling policies.

Graphic performance improvements

The headline feature of Parallels Desktop 27 is a new Metal-based graphics driver that delivers hardware-accelerated OpenGL 4.3 support to Windows virtual machines on Apple silicon, something Parallels says is unique among Mac virtualization tools right now. OpenGL 4.3 is the minimum graphics level required by many professional Windows apps. ArcGIS Pro, ZWCAD, and Blender 4.3 can now run in a virtualized environment on macOS thanks to this enhancement.

Parallels claims up to 160% faster OpenGL graphics performance on M3 and newer Macs. While boasting up to 35% faster 3D rendering in ArcGIS Pro, which cuts overall workflow time by up to 24%.

Better OpenGL support doesn’t just help professional engineering software. It helps anything that leans on that graphics stack, including games. I’m gaming on a PC for the first time in 20 years right now, all of it in a Windows VM on my M5 Pro, and it’s been incredible as I’ve been testing Parallels Desktop 27.

Local AI development gets faster

Parallels Desktop 27 also adds support for Scalable Matrix Extension (SME2) instructions in Linux and Windows VMs on M4 and newer Macs. Parallels notes that this translates to up to 7x faster AI and machine learning matrix operations and up to 1.75x faster neural network inference, with better performance for tools like Ollama and llama.cpp running inside a VM. For developers who want to build and test AI workloads locally rather than using cloud credits for every prompt, that’s a nice upgrade and further highlights the importance of Apple Silicon in the AI era.

What’s new for IT?

 Parallels Desktop for Enterprise now lets you use the CLI to determine whether a copy was activated with a license key or SSO, enabling organizations on Jamf to build extension attributes based on that for device management and reporting.

With the release of Desktop 27, Parallels also renewed its SOC 2 compliance. On top of that, Secure Golden Images Provisioning now supports distributing approved VM images via enterprise storage, including Azure Blob Storage and SharePoint, and includes improved declarative deployment for fully provisioned, zero-touch Windows VMs. For deploying at scale, this is important.

title: MacBook Lock aims to keep your laptop safe in coffee shops
snippet: Years ago, MacBooks incorporated a slot for using a cable lock to secure the device to a table leg or similar. They were most useful in coffee shops when you wanted to return to the counter to order another drink without having to carry your laptop with you. Those slots are long gone, but you can now buy adapters to secure your MacBook Neo, MacBook Air or MacBook Pro …
fullText:
Years ago, MacBooks incorporated a slot for using a cable lock to secure the device to a table leg or similar. They were most useful in coffee shops when you wanted to return to the counter to order another drink without having to carry your laptop with you.

Those slots are long gone, but you can now buy adapters to secure your MacBook Neo, MacBook Air or MacBook Pro …

You have to have been a relatively long-term MacBook user to remember the security slots embedded into the sides of the machines. These were designed for T-shaped attachments that were inserted through the slot, turned 90 degrees, and then locked into place. The most common design was a cable loop which could be passed around a table leg in a coffee shop or library.

CompuLock has now revived the idea with adapters that can be attached to the corner or edge of your MacBook in order to allow cable locks to be attached. They have a two-part construction with screws that enable the adapter to clamp to your MacBook.

The company has now added a MacBook Neo version to the existing models for the MacBook Air and MacBook Pro.

It should be stressed that these locks have only ever been very low-security devices, intended only to prevent someone quickly grabbing your MacBook and walking off with it in the space of a few seconds. I was happy enough to use one in smaller coffee shops, where I could still see my table while going to the counter for another cup of tea, but would never rely on one to let my MacBook out of my sight.

The adapters aren’t cheap at $70, given that you will still need to buy the lock itself, but if you have one laying around in a drawer, then you might consider it worth dusting off.

fullText:
Apple implemented a Siri AI waitlist for beta users of its upcoming operating systems, and it appears the same will be true when iOS 27 and macOS 27 officially launch next month.

This means that you won’t have immediate access to the new Siri AI features when your devices update to their new OS … 

Apple implemented a Siri AI waitlist in the first developer betas of both iOS 27 and macOS 27. This was likely done to allow the company to assess usage and therefore determine the server capacity required for AI tasks that can’t be carried-out on-device.

The amount of time beta users had to wait varied, with many reporting somewhere in the 1-2 week range. In the meantime, the setting for Siri AI simply read “Joined Waitlist.”

It looks like the Siri AI waitlist will be incorporated into the release versions of the new operating systems. A MacRumors forum member spotted that the company has just added code intended to provide an estimate of how long you may need to wait.

In Beta 7 across OS releases, Apple added new infrastructure to support personalized wait time messages set by a server after a user joins the Siri AI waitlist.

The time estimate is provided by the server, meaning that Apple can vary the timings depending on the balance of demand and capacity.

You’ll receive a pushed message once you’ve been given access to the shiny new features.

Good morning and happy Tuesday. It’s the perfect time to read conspiracies about who exactly made the new Ox Alpha AI model, cry about coffee getting even more expensive, add this fun daily typing challenge to your morning routine, and listen to r/indieheads’ top 106 songs of 2010 to 2026.

Inbox is written by Daniel Bader. Read previous issues here, and then catch up with Ben Schoon’s excellent Weekender column published every Sunday.

⭐️ Starred

I’ve owned every phone Google’s ever had a hand in, from the original Nexus One to the heavily subsidized Nexus 5 to the iconic Pixel 6 all the way to today’s Pixel 11. The early days of the Nexus were largely about buying a commodity piece of hardware built by a trusted manufacturing partner — often Samsung, LG, Huawei, or Motorola — and imbuing it with Google’s tasteful (and bloatware-free) build of Android.

	

But in 2014, with the debut of the Nexus 6 (aka The Whale), Google started experimenting with HDR+ bracketing, and over the years became the de facto leader in computational photography. Now the photo you take on any phone runs through a similar pipeline of multi-frame ingestion, bracketing, sharpening, color correction, and de-noising until it spits out something that may barely resemble the scene you actually framed.

Recently, as AI has infiltrated the photo-taking and editing process, we’ve seen strong pushback from phone users, particularly young ones, who are keen to embrace a more true-to-life aesthetic. Not only have mid-2000s digicams exploded in popularity, but apps like ZeroCam and ProShot on Android, and Halide on iOS, have become common downloads for many would-be photographers.

A few generations after Apple introduced Photographic Styles for its iPhones, Google’s Camera Looks feature takes a broader approach, with fewer specific filters (10 in total compared to Apple’s 15) but more ways to customize them: shadows, highlights, vibrance, sharpness, grain, tint, and warmth. As with all new Google products, Camera Looks has its quirks, but it’s a step in the right direction for people who demonstrably want less processing and more control over the photos they take.

For me, a Pixel phone’s greatest strength has always been how opinionated Google is about the way an owner should use its software. But in recent years, the company has eschewed the contrasty palette of early HDR+ for a more uniform, vibrant, and flat photo output that usually looks good but lacks distinctiveness. This is Google’s way of course-correcting, and while it’s not perfect, it’s a good start.

Read more: Camera Looks on the Pixel 11 delivers what I’ve wanted from Google’s photos for years

✉️ Inbox

Google’s inevitable ‘Pixel Watch Ultra’ should copy the Fitbit Air. Ben’s Weekender column is wish fulfillment over a sports-centric Pixel Watch, but personally I think Google should just make a more accurate Fitbit.

Samsung confirms August 27 event for the ‘newest addition to the Galaxy S26 family’. Samsung’s $649 Galaxy S25 FE is getting an update, and I’m hoping its biggest new feature isn’t “price increase.”

Pixel 11’s Magic Capture perfectly solves a very modern parenting dilemma. My column about how the Pixel’s Magic Capture is a solid solution for those moments when you don’t know whether you want to use your phone camera’s photo or video. #whynotboth

Galaxy Tab S12 series reportedly gets a price hike, but it’s not as bad as it could be. Yes, it’s as bad as it could be. Who’s paying these prices for an Android tablet?

Peloton brings its strength training app to Android after nearly two years on iPhone. Strength+ is the latest former iOS exclusive to be ported to Android, and it poses the question: was it Codex or Claude?

Google Home update lets you set light color temperature to your favorite kelvin using voice commands. My favorite Kelvin is Klein, which means all my lights are either black or white.

Pixel Watch 5’s AI watch face generator keeps the same form factor feeling fresh. I love this weird new addition to the Pixel Watch 5’s repertoire. I just wish I could use it on the phone instead of fiddling around on the watch itself.

Walmart finally supporting in-store tap to pay with Google Pay. The world’s biggest retailer finally caved and will now support Google Pay, Samsung Pay, and Apple Pay in its stores. All hail NFC and shared standards.

YouTube Premium is getting another price hike for some users all around the world. The objectively best subscription is getting an objectively terrible price hike in parts of Europe and Asia. A similar hike came to the US earlier this year.

Samsung reportedly bringing this major redesign back from the dead with Galaxy S27 [Gallery]. I’m excited for a Galaxy S27 that doesn’t look identical to the Galaxy S26, S25, S24, S23, and S22.

What is the ‘Android Pulse’ app that just appeared in Google Play Store updates? I love a good Android mystery.

Android brands struggle in Europe amidst RAMageddon, with Apple catching up. Low-end Android phones are getting more expensive, so people are just caving and buying more expensive phones, which is good news for Apple.

GrapheneOS phone from Motorola arrives next year, ‘higher end’ compared to Pixel with a price to match. Graphene’s first non-Google phone is a confusing partnership with Motorola, but more choice is good.

GrapheneOS support coming to Motorola Razr Fold & Ultra next year, Pixel 11 series too

Waze alerts are coming to navigation in Rivian’s electric vehicles. One more reason to lust after the Rivian R2.

Philips Hue’s new, cheaper Sync hardware leaks with ‘Camera’ and ‘Box Lite’ [Gallery]. I love Hue products and have many lightbulbs around my house, but their prices have recently pushed me to competing brands like Govee. Happy to see a potential price drop coming.

Gemini on Pixel 11 Pro testing ‘Device help’ tool

 🤑 Action items

It didn’t take long for someone to vibe-code a solution to the Pixel 11’s barebones HiLight feature.

I’ve been using the HiLight Studio app for the past few days and it’s actually been quite helpful. I was out for dinner the other day and had my Pixel 11 face-down on the table. I had set HiLight to pulse green when receiving a message from Beeper, and a few minutes later saw it light up. I didn’t know who messaged me until I turned on the screen, but maybe that’ll come in a future update.

More striking than the app itself — whose existence by no means obviates Google’s lackluster feature set — is how quickly it arrived. The author admits that it’s vibe-coded, which likely made it possible to develop at all. And now we’re in an environment where anyone can develop a specialty app for a small number of people or use cases, filling in usability gaps in the ecosystem or augmenting apps whose iOS versions were superior to their Android counterparts.

If you’re a developer working on a specialized app like HiLight Studio, give me a shout and I’ll feature it in an upcoming newsletter.

title: Americans Want to Know When Their Healthcare Providers Use AI
snippet: AI chatbots are changing the healthcare landscape, but privacy and transparency remain critical concerns.
fullText:
AI chatbots are being used in healthcare, both in and out of the doctor’s office, more than ever before. Patients and medical providers alike are turning to AI for treatments and diagnoses, but transparency remains a key concern, a new survey by Pew Research Center shows. 

A poll of 3,488 US adults conducted between June 22 and June 28 found that a quarter of respondents use chatbots to diagnose symptoms. Those turning to chatbots for health mainly cite convenience and affordability as their motive. Patients also use AI chatbots to find information quickly and at no cost, better understand a doctor’s diagnosis, interpret lab results and decide whether to seek in-person care.

Of these survey participants, almost half (47%) say the health information generated by the chatbot was “extremely” helpful, and 48% said the information was “somewhat” helpful. Only 5% said the results were not too helpful or not at all helpful.

AI chatbots work by simulating a conversation between two parties and responding to your prompts or inputs using the massive amounts of information the models were trained on. Many people appreciate the convenience they offer, as chatbots are available 24/7 and can often be accessed for free and sometimes without an account. Chatbots, however, are known to “hallucinate,” or generate false information in their responses, which can be particularly dangerous or alarming when your personal health is in question. Among other issues, they’re trained to produce a probable answer, not necessarily one grounded in truth, and they’re likely to sound particularly confident about that answer.

But generative artificial intelligence is also showing up at the doctor’s office — and Pew found that Americans have greater concerns about its use there.

Read also: ChatGPT Health Will See You Now, and It’s a Big Step Forward for Medical Queries

When doctors turn to chatbots

While recent numbers show that about one in three US adults have used chatbots for health-related questions, medical providers are also increasingly turning to AI in the office for note-taking, interpreting exams and more. 

While views on AI use in doctors’ offices vary, one factor remains of critical concern to patients: transparency. 

Of those surveyed, 72% say it is “extremely or very important” for their medical provider to disclose any use of AI. The survey also found that a vast majority of people (eight in 10) want to be told if AI is being used directly for care or medical decisions, such as diagnoses and the analysis of scans, X-rays and lab results. AI is frequently used for triage purposes — and has even been shown to outperform human ER doctors — as well as to complete clinical tasks more quickly. For instance, AI has been used effectively to reduce the window of X-ray interpretations from 11.2 to 2.7 days. 

Although Americans want advance notice when AI is used in their healthcare, nearly half (47%) are unsure whether it has ever played a role in their treatment, underscoring limited awareness of when, where and how the technology is used.

Americans are not fully comfortable with AI

The survey shows that Americans may find AI chatbots convenient, but not entirely trustworthy. 

Views are mixed on sharing personal health histories and diagnoses with AI. Among those surveyed, 29% say they are extremely or very comfortable sharing health information with chatbots, while 26% say they are uncomfortable doing so.

The findings suggest that although AI is increasingly used for health information and care, public confidence and understanding have not kept pace with its adoption.

title: Apple could debut two AirPods 5 models next month, per report
snippet: Although AirPods with cameras aren’t expected until next year, Bloomberg reports that Apple could announce the AirPods 5 as early as next month’s expected iPhone event. Here are the details.
fullText:
Although AirPods with cameras aren’t expected until next year, Bloomberg reports that Apple could announce the AirPods 5 as early as next month’s expected iPhone event. Here are the details.

AirPods 5 to feature regular and ANC variants

In a wide-ranging report published earlier tonight, Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman said Apple could announce a new Mac mini in the coming days, ahead of its expected September event.

Gurman also detailed several other products Apple has in the pipeline, including the AirPods 5, which could debut as early as next month. He says the company’s next event is expected to take place on September 9 and will also feature its first foldable iPhone, the iPhone 18 Pro lineup, and new Apple Watches.

From the report:

The company is also preparing a range of new Apple Watches with minor changes, including upgrades to fitness tracking and a ceramic-case option for Series 12 models. And it’s planning to debut fresh AirPods as early as the September product launch event.

The rollout will include new AirPods 5, an update to Apple’s entry-level earbuds, the people said. That model was last refreshed in 2024. A camera-equipped version of the AirPods, meanwhile, isn’t expected until next year.

Interestingly, Gurman followed up on his own report with a post on X, adding that the AirPods 5 are expected to come in both regular and noise-cancellation variants:

Also in this story: While the camera AirPods aren’t coming until next year, there should still be new Apple earbuds this year: the AirPods 5 in both regular and noise-cancelation flavors. https://t.co/eTsSTbJ3op

— Mark Gurman (@markgurman) August 25, 2026

While reporting on the AirPods 5 timeline has been scarce, the earbuds had generally been expected to arrive in 2027. Apple is also reportedly developing two camera-equipped AirPods models that will use Visual Intelligence and Siri for AI-powered features.

Apple recently mistakenly included a demo video of the camera-equipped AirPods in the macOS 26.7 release candidate, though the clip didn’t clearly show what was physically different about the device.
